title: Strike, catch and merge two balls
summary: Two small balls wait behind closed shutters near the top of two parallel inclined lanes. The shutters open by themselves, the first shortly after the start and the second a few seconds later, and each released ball rolls down its lane and flies off the open lower end. The left Panda's paddle must touch each ball after the ball has flown free. The right Panda's cup must catch the first ball and carry it away from the catch point without losing it. The cup must then catch the second ball while still holding the first, and finally put both balls into a fixed basin, where they must come to rest with the cup no longer touching them.
robot_setup: panda-0 (left): base at (-0.55, -0.22, 0), yaw 0 (facing +x). It carries a flat rigid paddle, 0.14 m long (2 x `tool_half`, `tool_half` = 0.07 m), 0.05 m tall and 12 mm thick. A side adapter runs forward from the hand and then sideways to the paddle's -y end. The tool frame is the paddle's centre, with x normal to its faces, y along its length and z up. The hand's TCP sits 0.12 m behind the paddle centre (tool -x), 0.14 m to the tool -y side and 0.04 m above it. Start: paddle centre at (0.10, -0.21, 0.22), orientation identity (faces normal to world x, length along world y). panda-1 (right): base at (0.74, 0.22, 0), yaw pi (facing -x). It carries an open-top square cup, 0.14 m x 0.14 m inside (2 x `tool_half`), with four 0.055 m high, 5 mm thick walls and a 5 mm floor, held by an adapter on its tool -x wall. The tool frame is the centre of the cup floor's inner surface, z up out of the cup. The TCP sits 0.12 m along tool -x and 0.04 m above the tool frame. Start: cup frame at (0.19, 0.17, 0.18), quaternion (0, 0, 0, 1) (yawed 180 deg: tool x = world -x, tool y = world -y, cup upright). Role labels (panda-0 / panda-1) by phase: first_redirect striker / receiver; first_catch cleared_striker / catcher; loaded_cup_relocation preparing_striker / loaded_carrier; second_redirect striker / loaded_receiver; second_catch cleared_striker / two_ball_catcher; both_delivery cleared_partner / deliverer.
scene: Two identical small orange balls (radius 16 mm) start at rest: ball1 in the lane on the -y side, ball2 in the lane on the +y side. Each lane is a straight grey gravity channel with a 70 mm wide, low-friction floor and 22 mm side walls. The lanes are open at both ends, stand on posts above the table and slope down toward +x. Near the upper end of each lane an amber shutter blocks the ball, and a small fixed housing block stands beside each shutter. The shutters are motor-driven and lift by themselves: ball1's shutter opens shortly after the start and ball2's a few seconds later (the exact time varies from instance to instance). Each released ball rolls down its lane and leaves the lower end in free flight. A fixed blue open-top basin, 0.16 m x 0.16 m inside and 0.075 m deep, stands on posts above the table. Nothing else moves by itself. The table top is the world's z = 0 plane.
scene_privileged: Balls ball1 and ball2: radius 0.016 m, mass 0.025 kg (hard-coded; `object_mass` is not used), restitution 0.1, friction 0.2. At reset both are placed at rest at (-0.19, y, 0.377), y = -0.09 for ball1 and y = +0.09 for ball2, on the lane floor just upstream of the shutter. Lanes lane0 (y = -0.09) and lane1 (y = +0.09) are static gravity channels. Each floor's top surface runs from (-0.22, y, 0.37) down to (0.06, y, `lane_end_z`) = (0.06, y, 0.28), a slope of about 17.8 deg. Floor half-width 0.035 m; side walls 8 mm thick and 0.022 m high, centred at +-0.039 m from the lane axis; friction 0.1; both ends open. `lane_end_jitter` = 0, so no lane draw is made. Release gates gate0 and gate1 are prismatic shutters, 10 mm (x) x 58 mm (y) x 50 mm (z), with their lower edge at (-0.16, y, 0.358). They lift along world +z with 0 to 0.06 m of travel. Each gate's fixed housing block (36 x 28 x 70 mm) sits 0.09 m to the +y side of its shutter. Gate drive: PD with kp 60, kd 6 and a 3 N force limit. Each gate is held closed (target 0) until its release time t_i. After that its target rises as 0.22 x (t - t_i) m (velocity target 0.22 m/s) until the 0.06 m limit. Release times: t_1 = `first_release` = 0.25 s (`first_release_jitter` = 0, no draw). t_2 = `second_release` + U(-`second_release_jitter`, +`second_release_jitter`) = 3.8 + U(-0.12, 0.12) s, drawn at reset (stored in flag `release_times`, not in the observation). Basin: static container with floor top surface centre at (0.20, 0.32, 0.08); inner half-size 0.08 x 0.08 m; wall height 0.075 m (rim at z = 0.155); 5 mm walls; friction 0.4; restitution 0.03. Tools: `tool_half` = 0.07 for both, `tool_mass` = 0.2 kg, `tool_friction` = 0.3, tool restitution 0.05. `table_friction` = 0.08. Horizon `horizon` = 25 s. `radius` = 0.016 is the radius used by the predicates. Unused here: `incoming_speed`, `fixture_speed`, `preview`, `restitution`, `object_mass`. The only random draw is the t_2 offset.

phases.name: first_redirect
phases.text: At some moment during this phase, ball1 has flown free (touching nothing at all) for more than 0.025 s. After that, it touches the left paddle (panda-0's tool). Where the ball goes after the touch is not checked.

phases.name: first_catch
phases.text: ball1 enters the right cup (panda-1's tool) from above and is retained. The entry: after touching nothing for at least 0.025 s, the ball's centre passes downward through the plane 0.071 m above the cup floor (wall height 0.055 m + radius 0.016 m, in the cup's frame). At that crossing the centre must be within 0.054 m (`tool_half` - radius) of the cup centre along both cup x and cup y. From then on the ball must stay contained in the cup for 0.18 s without interruption. Contained in the cup means all of the following, in the cup's frame: |x| and |y| of the ball centre below 0.0628 m (`tool_half` - 0.45 x radius); height above the cup floor between 0.012 m and 0.0531 m; in contact with the cup within the last 25 ms; moving at less than 0.09 m/s relative to the cup (including the cup's rotation). The free-flight time counts only from the start of this phase. The cup's position when this phase completes is recorded as the catch position.

phases.name: loaded_cup_relocation
phases.text: With ball1 contained in the right cup (as defined in first_catch), the cup's tool-frame origin is more than 0.06 m from the recorded catch position.

phases.name: second_redirect
phases.text: At some moment during this phase, ball2 has flown free (touching nothing) for more than 0.025 s; only free flight while this phase is active counts. After that, ball2 touches the left paddle. Where the ball goes after the touch is not checked.

phases.name: second_catch
phases.text: ball2 enters the right cup from above and is retained exactly as in first_catch. That is: an entry after at least 0.025 s of free flight (counted from the start of this phase), crossing downward through the plane 0.071 m above the cup floor within 0.054 m of the cup centre on both axes, then contained in the cup for 0.18 s without interruption. At that moment ball1 must also be contained in the cup.

phases.name: both_delivery
phases.text: Both balls are contained in the basin and neither touches the cup, for 0.7 s without interruption. Contained in the basin means all of the following, in the basin's frame (origin at the centre of its floor's top surface, axes = world axes): |x| and |y| of the ball centre below 0.0728 m (0.08 - 0.45 x radius); height above the basin floor between 0.012 m and 0.0731 m; in contact with the basin within the last 25 ms; speed below 0.09 m/s. This completes the task.

task_failures: first_ball_spill: during loaded_cup_relocation, second_redirect and second_catch, ball1's centre leaves the cup's interior footprint or drops low. In the right cup's frame, that is |x| or |y| greater than 0.07 m (`tool_half`), or more than 0.01 m below the cup floor surface.
contact_rules: The paddle and the cup may touch only the two balls. Neither tool may touch the lanes or their support posts, the shutters or their housing blocks, the basin or its posts, the table, or the robot pedestals. No other robot part, the fingers included, may touch anything. The two arms and their tools must never touch each other, and a tool must not touch its own arm.
world_goals_fixed: All goal geometry is relative to the cup, the paddle or the basin.
world_goals_seeded: `goal_target` = (0.22, 0.02, 0.18) is announced at reset in the observation, but no phase condition uses it.
difficulty_note: The balls arrive on a schedule the robot cannot change: the first strike, catch and loaded relocation must fit before the second shutter opens. The second catch must then take a ball deflected by the paddle into a cup that already holds the first ball, without spilling it.
standard_notes: At t = 0 both balls are still at rest behind their shutters. The first shutter opens a fraction of a second later, so ball1 is rolling almost immediately. The second shutter opens on its own a few seconds later, whether or not the first ball has been handled.
